key_insight: SELDON uses a continuous-time deep ODE variational model to learn supernova explosion dynamics from irregular light curves, producing millisecond-scale, amortized posterior inference that replaces hours-long MCMC runs. This enables real-time parameter estimation and uncertainty quantification at LSST alert scales.
problem_solved: How to perform fast, accurate, and uncertainty-aware inference of transient (supernova) parameters from irregularly sampled light curves when alert rates (∼10 million/night) make traditional physics-based MCMC pipelines infeasible.
method: Continuous-time variational autoencoder built around neural ODE latent dynamics to model light-curve evolution in continuous time.
Amortized inference (encoder → latent ODE → decoder) for millisecond-scale posterior predictions and calibrated uncertainty estimates.
End-to-end training on simulated/observed transient light curves to handle irregular sampling and deliver scalable, real-time inference.
impact: Enables scalable, real-time transient parameter inference and uncertainty quantification for Rubin LSST-scale alert streams, allowing rapid follow-up prioritization and resource allocation. Provides a practical blueprint for ML practitioners building continuous-time, amortized inference systems for scientific time series.
